title: The password was rotated correctly, and the app locked itself out
intro: A scheduled rotation changed the shop application's database password at 02:00: the new password was set in the database and written to Vault, as the runbook says. At 02:00 the app's error rate went to 100%: 'password authentication failed for user shop_app'. Vault holds the secret at secret/shop/database. An ExternalSecret named shop-db syncs it into a Kubernetes Secret of the same name in namespace shop, and the deployment shop reads it as the environment variable DB_PASSWORD.

steps.prompt: Follow the secret from its source to the app, one hop at a time. First, Vault: check the metadata of secret/shop/database to see its versions and when they were written.
expected_commands: vault kv metadata get secret/shop/database
vault kv metadata get -mount=secret shop/database
steps.fake_output:
========== Metadata ==========
current_version    5
updated_time       2026-09-28T02:00:04Z

====== Version 5 ======
created_time    2026-09-28T02:00:04Z
====== Version 4 ======
created_time    2026-09-21T09:14:02Z

steps.prompt: Vault has version 5, written at 02:00. Next hop: has the ExternalSecret shop-db in namespace shop synced since then?
expected_commands: kubectl get externalsecret shop-db -n shop
kubectl get es shop-db -n shop
kubectl get externalsecrets shop-db -n shop
kubectl describe externalsecret shop-db -n shop
steps.fake_output:
NAME      STORE   REFRESH INTERVAL   STATUS         READY   LAST SYNC
shop-db   vault   1h                 SecretSynced   True    2026-09-28T02:41:10Z

steps.prompt: It synced at 02:41, after the rotation. So the Kubernetes Secret should hold the new value. Read the first 6 characters of the password key in Secret shop-db, enough to compare without printing it all.
expected_commands: kubectl get secret shop-db -n shop -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d | cut -c1-6
kubectl get secret shop-db -n shop -o jsonpath="{.data.password}" | base64 -d | cut -c1-6
kubectl get secret shop-db -n shop -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 --decode | cut -c1-6
steps.hint: kubectl get secret shop-db -n shop -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d | cut -c1-6

steps.prompt: That's the start of the new password. Last hop: what does the running app have? Print the first 6 characters of DB_PASSWORD inside the deployment's pod.
expected_commands: kubectl exec -n shop deployment/shop -- sh -c 'echo $DB_PASSWORD | cut -c1-6'
kubectl exec deployment/shop -n shop -- sh -c 'echo $DB_PASSWORD | cut -c1-6'
kubectl exec -n shop deploy/shop -- sh -c 'echo $DB_PASSWORD | cut -c1-6'
kubectl exec -n shop deployment/shop -- sh -c "echo \$DB_PASSWORD | cut -c1-6"
steps.hint: kubectl exec -n shop deployment/shop -- sh -c 'echo $DB_PASSWORD | cut -c1-6'

steps.prompt: Different. The pod still has the old password: environment variables are fixed when a container starts, and these pods started last week. Restart the deployment so new pods read the current Secret.
expected_commands: kubectl rollout restart deployment/shop -n shop
kubectl rollout restart deployment shop -n shop
kubectl rollout restart deploy/shop -n shop
kubectl rollout restart deploy shop -n shop

steps.prompt: Wait for the rollout to finish.
expected_commands: kubectl rollout status deployment/shop -n shop
kubectl rollout status deployment shop -n shop
kubectl rollout status deploy/shop -n shop
steps.fake_output:
Waiting for deployment "shop" rollout to finish: 2 of 3 updated replicas are available...
deployment "shop" successfully rolled out

resolution: The rotation runbook changed the password in two places, the database and Vault, and stopped. The secret then had three more hops to make before the application had it, and each has its own delay. Vault to the Kubernetes Secret: the ExternalSecret refreshes hourly, so for up to an hour (41 minutes here) the cluster still held the old value. The Kubernetes Secret to the pod: never, without a restart, because the app reads it as an environment variable, and those are set once when the container starts. Meanwhile the database had dropped the old password at 02:00 sharp. So the app was locked out the instant the rotation ran and would have stayed that way until someone restarted it. Following the value hop by hop, comparing a few characters at each, found exactly where it stopped moving. There are two ways to make rotation safe, and good setups use both. Make propagation automatic and fast: trigger a sync after writing to Vault, and restart consumers when their Secret changes (Reloader does this), or mount secrets as files and have the app re-read them. And never have a moment when only one password works: rotate with two valid credentials. Create the new one alongside the old, roll it out everywhere, confirm nothing uses the old one, and only then remove it. For databases that means two users that alternate, or Vault's dynamic credentials, where each instance has its own short-lived user and there's nothing shared to rotate. A runbook whose last step is 'write the new value' isn't finished; the last step is 'confirm every consumer is using it'.
